topics.label: Introduction to cancer hallmarks and lecture overview
topics.groupedBecause: It frames the lecture by outlining the learning outcomes and introducing the conceptual framework of cancer hallmarks.

topics.label: Growth signal autonomy and signaling pathway mutations
topics.groupedBecause: They describe how oncogenic mutations in cell-surface receptor pathways, including Wnt and receptor tyrosine kinases, drive constitutive proliferation and cell survival.

topics.label: Block to terminal differentiation in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: They examine how malignant transformation disrupts normal maturation and arrests terminal differentiation in hematopoietic lineages and the intestinal epithelium.

topics.label: Evasion of apoptosis, replicative immortality, and p53 regulation
topics.groupedBecause: They explain how cancer cells overcome intrinsic barriers to unlimited growth by resisting apoptosis, bypassing telomere-driven senescence, and disabling p53-mediated stress responses.

topics.label: Cancer metabolic rewiring and oncometabolites
topics.groupedBecause: They introduce complex cancer hallmarks and describe how altered cellular metabolism, the Warburg effect, and oncometabolites drive tumorigenesis.

topics.label: Induction of tumor angiogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: It explains the requirement of new blood vessel formation for tumor nutrient supply and how the balance of activators and inhibitors controls the angiogenic switch.

topics.label: Mechanisms, detection, and genomics of tumor metastasis
topics.groupedBecause: They examine the biological barriers to metastatic dissemination, the utility of circulating tumor cells as biomarkers, and the genomic features supporting distant colonization.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and summary
topics.groupedBecause: It concludes the lecture with a summary of the hallmarks of cancer and closing remarks.
